key_insight: Conditioning the decoder as well as the denoising network preserves structural detail and temporal consistency in video generation; a reference-conditioned decoder (RefDecoder) significantly reduces detail loss and mismatch to the input image.
problem_solved: Latent diffusion-based video generation systems typically use heavily conditioned denoisers but leave decoders unconditional, causing loss of fine detail and visual inconsistency relative to reference frames or input images.
method: Introduce RefDecoder: a decoder module that receives explicit conditioning from reference frames and temporal/contextual features (e.g., cross-attention or feature fusion) to guide reconstruction.
Integrate RefDecoder into a latent diffusion pipeline so both denoising and decoding stages are conditioned, preserving structure across time.
Train with reconstruction and temporal-consistency objectives (e.g., perceptual/LPIPS losses and frame-consistency losses) to enforce fidelity and smoothness.
impact: Equalizing conditioning between denoiser and decoder yields higher-fidelity, more consistent video outputs, improving controllability for editing and downstream tasks while reducing artifacts—easy to adopt in existing latent diffusion pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: latent diffusion encoder + conditioned denoiser + RefDecoder with cross-attention to reference frames (highlighting the added conditioning path).
Side-by-side comparison: generated frames from standard pipeline vs. RefDecoder (showing improved detail and consistency).
Attention / feature-flow visualization: how reference features influence decoding over time (heatmaps or flow arrows).
Metrics chart: improvements on fidelity and consistency metrics (e.g., FID, LPIPS, temporal consistency) across baselines.
paper_title: RefDecoder: Enhancing Visual Generation with Conditional Video Decoding
paper_authors: Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Bohan Fang, Zhongzheng Ren, Ranjay Krishna
